paper_sections.title: Post-traumatic stress symptoms correlate with smaller subgenual cingulate, caudate, and insula volumes in unmedicated combat veterans
3.3.1. Covariation for combat exposure, depressive symptoms, and age

description.value: The study examined whether post-traumatic stress symptom severity and trauma exposure were associated with regional gray matter volume in combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans, using dimensional regression and PTSD versus non-PTSD group comparisons.

design.value: Cross-sectional structural MRI study of 28 combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans, including 13 participants with PTSD and 15 without PTSD. Voxel-based morphometry was used to analyze gray matter volume, first dimensionally by regression against total CAPS score and childhood and adult trauma load, and subsequently by diagnostic group contrast.

name.value: standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template

description.value: Past month post-traumatic stress symptoms were assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale. Total CAPS score and B, C, and D symptom subscores were used; full PTSD criteria were identified using the F1/I2 criteria.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I)

description.value: Subjects were assessed with the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders to identify major concurrent psychiatric disorders.
Depressive symptom severity was measured using the Beck Depression Inventory.
Level of combat exposure was measured with the Combat Exposure Scale.

A self-report measure of exposure to a wide variety of traumas, including the number of times an event occurred and age at the time of exposure. The number of trauma types experienced before and after age 18 was summed to indicate childhood and adult trauma load, respectively.

description.value: Twenty-eight combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans, 25 males and 3 females, were recruited from the Pittsburgh area through public media advertisements.

inclusion_criteria.value: prior military service documented with DD Form 214

exclusion_criteria.value: history of traumatic brain injury or neurological disease
current (past month) alcohol or illicit substance abuse or dependence
use of greater than 14 alcoholic drinks per week over the past month and confirmed on prospective diaries
failure to meet screening criteria for MRI
possibility of pregnancy for women of child-bearing age

one subject also met criteria for generalized anxiety disorder in the past month

clinical_characteristics.value: Thirteen subjects met full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria. One subject also met criteria for generalized anxiety disorder in the past month. No other concurrent psychiatric illnesses were identified.

task_description.value: Structural brain magnetic resonance imaging was obtained from combat veterans and analyzed using voxel-based morphometry.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Siemens Trio MRI scanner (Siemens, Malvern, PA) at the University of Pittsburgh Magnetic Resonance Research Center

description.value: Three-dimensional sagittal high-resolution MPRAGE scans were acquired with echo time = 2.98 ms, repetition time = 2300 ms, slice thickness = 1.2 mm, 160 slices, flip angle = 9°, field of view = 256 × 240 mm, inversion time = 900 ms, and image matrix = 256 × 240 covering the entire brain.

DICOM files were converted to NIFTI-1 format, segmented into gray and white matter, and normalized to the standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template using a unified model integrated within SPM8. Voxel values were modulated by Jacobian determinants derived from spatial normalization. The final voxel resolution after normalization was 2 × 2 × 2 mm. Images were smoothed with a 12-mm Gaussian kernel; for analysis of the hippocampus only, images were smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: DICOM files were converted to NIFTI-1 format.
Converted files were segmented into gray and white matter.
Images were normalized to the standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template using a unified model integrated within SPM8.
Voxel values were modulated by the Jacobian determinants derived from spatial normalization.
The final voxel resolution after normalization was 2 × 2 × 2 mm.
Images were smoothed with a 12-mm Gaussian kernel.
For analysis of the hippocampus only, images were smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: Regressors included the total past-month CAPS score, childhood trauma load, and adult trauma load. All images were covaried for total gray matter volume as determined by Easy Volume. Regional GMV findings were considered significant for uncorrected P < 0.001 at the voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels.
Extracted cluster averages adjusted for total GMV were analyzed with CES scores, BDI scores, and age added as additional regressors.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), version 18

model_settings.value: Normalized cluster averages were entered into a multivariate regression with CAPS symptom subscores: B, re-experiencing; C, avoidance/numbing; and D, hyperarousal. Bonferroni correction was applied based on the number of clusters examined, P < 0.05/4 or 0.013.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), version 18

model_settings.value: Subjects were divided into diagnostic groups of PTSD (n = 13) and non-PTSD (n = 15), with total GMV as a covariate. Regional GMV findings were considered significant for uncorrected P < 0.001 at the voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels.

interpretations.value: The consistency of findings using these two methods suggests the utility of whole brain correlation with symptom dimensions beyond diagnostic groups.

footer.value: Values represent either count (percent) or mean (standard deviation). Values in bold are statistically different between the PTSD and non-PTSD groups, two-tailed t-test, P < 0.05. CAPS = Clinician-administered PTSD Scale (past month).

description.value: Demographic and clinical variables for the PTSD and non-PTSD groups.

caption.value: Summary of smaller gray matter volume associated with greater post-traumatic stress symptoms (↑CAPS, ↓GMV), greater child trauma load (↑Child Trauma, ↓GMV), or PTSD compared to non-PTSD. Regions shown were significant at uncorrected P < 0.001, threshold k = 50 voxels. k = cluster size. CAPS = Clinician-administered PTSD Scale. GMV = gray matter volume. Peak coordinates based on Montreal Neurological Institute atlas.
